baseline_manifest_entry.title: Finite lacunary exponential sums belong to BMO
baseline_manifest_entry.statement:
Let $0<a\le b<\infty$, and let $(\xi_n)_{n\in\mathbb Z}$ be nonzero real
frequencies satisfying
$a2^n\le|\xi_n|\le b2^n$ for every $n$. Let $(c_n)_{n\in\mathbb Z}$ have
finite support and put
$$f(x):=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}c_ne^{2\pi i\xi_nx}.$$
Then
$$\|f\|_{\mathrm{BMO}(\mathbb R)}\le C_{a,b,\phi}\Bigl(\sum_n|c_n|^2\Bigr)^{1/2}.$$
More precisely, fix a nonnegative $\phi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$ with
$\phi\ge1$ on $[-\tfrac12,\tfrac12]$. For an interval $I$ of length $L$ and
centre $x_I$, set $\phi_I(x):=\phi((x-x_I)/L)$. There is a constant
$c_I\in\mathbb C$ such that
$$\int_{\mathbb R}\phi_I(x)|f(x)-c_I|^2\,dx
\le C_{a,b,\phi}L\sum_n|c_n|^2.$$

references.title: Terence Tao, Math 247A Lecture Notes 4 (UCLA, Fall 2006)
references.locator: Exercise Q4 (Lacunary exponential sums lie in BMO), printed pp. 26-27

baseline_manifest_entry.strategy: Split at the least integer n0 with 2^n0 >= |I|^{-1}. For n<n0 choose the value of the low-frequency sum at the centre of I; its weighted L2 oscillation is bounded by the geometric sum of |xi_n|^2. For n>=n0, expand the weighted square and use integration by parts in the fixed smooth bump to obtain rapid decay in L|xi_n-xi_m|. Frequency comparability gives uniformly bounded absolute row sums: finitely many nearby indices are harmless, higher indices form a geometric tail, and lower indices are bounded by r(1+c 2^r)^(-M). The Schur estimate gives the high-frequency L2 bound. The bump dominates I, so Cauchy-Schwarz and the optimal-constant BMO inequality give the claimed seminorm bound. Finite sums only; no choice principle is used.
